task: Extend the exact rational cycle/signing construction to arbitrary bipartite perfect-matching marginals, charge the graph/feature interface, and distinguish sampler from explicit support output.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For a rational feasible perfect-matching marginal x on a labelled bipartite graph and b=2^T, let q=bx, l_e=floor(q_e), r_e=q_e-l_e. Every residual degree sum_e incident to v r_e=b-sum_e incident to v l_e is an integer. In any state reached by alternating-cycle endpoint moves, a vertex cannot have exactly one fractional incident residual edge; hence nonempty fractional support contains an even cycle. Moving along its alternating incidence vector to either feasible interval endpoint and choosing the endpoints with probabilities t_+/(t_+-t_-) and -t_-/(t_+-t_-) preserves the conditional mean and every degree, and fixes at least one coordinate. After at most |E| moves, y_T=l+r is an integer degree-b b-matching with E[y_T]=bx and |y_T,e-bx_e|<1 per edge.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'Initial residual b-matching cycle rounder'; cycle2_bipartite_sampler.py::_initial_residual_bmatching
claims.novelty_boundary: The construction is a specialized cycle-rounding/dependent-rounding argument; no novelty or priority claim is made. The cited primary work is context, not the proof of the stated floor/ceiling interface.
claims.costs: At most |E| endpoint coins and cycle searches; all probabilities exact rationals. A common denominator Q for x is preserved by residual moves, so endpoint probabilities have O(L_x) bits. Cycle-search and update costs are polynomial in |V|, |E|, L_x, and T.
claims.falsifier: A reachable nonempty fractional residual graph with no even cycle, failure of integer residual degrees, an endpoint outside [0,1], or a nonzero expected cycle step.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof/code review of the residual cycle finder and exact endpoint transition.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: If y_t is a nonnegative integer bipartite b-matching of degree 2^t, t>=1, its odd-numerator edge graph is Eulerian because each vertex's incident multiplicity sum is even. Decompose that graph into edge-disjoint even cycles C; choose alternating directions delta_C. For rational feature columns A_e with ||A_e||_2<=1, put w_C=A delta_C and U_t=ceil max_C||w_C||_2. Li's deterministic rational signing on columns w_C/U_t returns signs s_C with ||sum_C s_C w_C||_infinity<99 U_t. An independent fair orientation eta and y_{t-1}=(y_t+eta sum_C s_C delta_C)/2 are feasible nonnegative integer degree-2^(t-1) b-matchings for both eta values and satisfy E[y_{t-1}|y_t]=y_t/2.
claims.status: internally proved conditional on source-reported Li signing theorem
claims.novelty_boundary: Li supplies the signing algorithm and constant; this report proves the cycle reduction, parity feasibility, and martingale conversion. No independent validation of Li's result is claimed.
claims.costs: At most |E| cycles per level and T signing calls along one sample. Exact cycle sums and integer U_t use polynomial-bit rational/integer arithmetic. Li reports deterministic polynomial bit complexity on rational inputs.
claims.falsifier: An odd-edge graph vertex of odd degree, a cycle move that changes a vertex degree or leaves an edge odd/negative for one orientation, or a signing output violating its exact 99U_t check.
claims.next_gate: Integrate or independently review a concrete Li implementation; measure cycle-scale growth on application-relevant feature maps.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For the exact sampler formed by the residual rounder and T cycle-coarsening levels, with A_e rational and ||A_e||_2<=1, each path P returns an actual perfect matching M with E[1_M]=x and ||A(1_M-x)||_infinity <= |E|2^-T + 99 sum_{t=1}^T 2^-t U_t(P). Hence every support atom is bounded by |E|2^-T+99 max_P sum_t 2^-t U_t(P). Since U_t<=|E|, a universal bound from the stated assumptions is |E|2^-T+99|E|, not a graph-independent constant.
claims.status: internally proved conditional on Li signing theorem
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, sections 'Result and interface', 'Odd-numerator cycle coarsening', and 'Bound, oracles, precision, and runtime'
claims.novelty_boundary: The pathwise bound keeps the realized cycle scales; it does not assert a dimension- or graph-independent discrepancy guarantee. The simpler |E| bound is intentionally conservative.
claims.costs: No optimization/separation oracle; input feasibility uses exact edge nonnegativity and degree checks. Initial residual uses O(|E|) rational moves. Each of T levels calls a polynomial-bit rational signer on at most |E| cycle columns. Expected fair random bits O(|E|L_x+T).
claims.falsifier: Any output path exceeding its computed exact path_bound or having a nonmatching incidence vector; a cycle feature norm exceeding |E| under unit-norm columns would falsify the coarse bound.
claims.next_gate: Test whether a target application has uniformly bounded cycle sums or supports sharper signing beyond unit-normalized cycle columns.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For every k>=1, let G=C_{2k}, take x_e=1/2 on all actual cycle edges, and give alternating edges actual scalar feature coefficients +1,-1. Then every edge column has norm one, the only perfect matchings have feature deviations +k and -k, and exact marginals force probability 1/2 on each. Therefore no universal graph-independent all-atom constant can hold for arbitrary unit-norm actual-edge features on general bipartite perfect-matching polytopes.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'Sharp lower bound on graph-independent feature control'
claims.novelty_boundary: This refutes a universal constant transfer for the stated feature model. It does not refute graph-size bounds, bounds under cycle-feature assumptions, or other feature classes.
claims.costs: The witness has 2k actual edges, two perfect matchings, scalar dimension one, and exact rational marginals/features.
claims.falsifier: An additional perfect matching on C_{2k}, or an exact-marginal law whose mass on either of the two matchings differs from 1/2; both contradict the explicit cycle structure and edge marginals.
claims.next_gate: Use cycle-feature norms, rather than edge-column norms alone, as a necessary assumption in any proposed constant-bound theorem.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: The exact finite sampler induces a finite rational law supported only on matchings satisfying its pathwise feature bound. Since x is in the convex hull of these safe matching incidence vectors, Caratheodory implies existence of a rational law on at most |E|+1 safe matchings with mean x; determinant bounds give polynomial weight bit length. The current implementation does not construct this compressed law in polynomial time; naive enumeration of all branching paths can be exponential in |E|+T.
claims.status: existence internally proved; efficient explicit-support extraction UNKNOWN
claims.novelty_boundary: This separates mathematical compressibility from an implemented algorithm. No polynomial-time compression claim is made.
claims.costs: Existence support size O(|E|); naive full sampler-tree enumeration has up to 2^(|E|+T) paths. Efficient extraction is not costed.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to finite Caratheodory compression within the sampler's safe atom set; conversely an explicit polynomial algorithm would resolve the extraction gate.
claims.next_gate: Investigate safe-atom column generation or direct polynomial support construction without expanding the full path tree.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: The Python wrapper was run on C4, C6, and C10 at center marginals with alternating scalar edge features and a valid one-column +1 signer. For both antipodal orientation outcomes it returned the two alternating perfect matchings with exact discrepancies +k and -k and path bounds that dominate those discrepancies.

claims.novelty_boundary: Finite wrapper checks do not validate Li's signing theorem or the universal proof.
claims.costs: Three small instances, exact Fraction arithmetic; the supplied signer is valid only for the one-column normalized cycle input in these fixtures.
claims.falsifier: A returned matching that is not one of the two alternating matchings, a discrepancy other than +/-k, or violation of the exact path certificate.
claims.next_gate: Retain as a regression test and add independent tests with multi-cycle odd-edge graphs and a production Li signer.
